# Singularity design system

> Components, tokens and rules for Singularity apps (`@singularityfm/design-system`). Pick a part here before writing a class or a value; a part that fits is used as it is, none fits means ask the owner. Never invent a control class.

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/system/build.ts (npm run system). Do not edit. -->
Ask `ds find "<need>"`, `ds part <id>` or `ds token <words>`, not this whole file (`pnpm exec ds` in an app, `pnpm run ds` here). Rules for an app: AGENTS.md. All pages in one file: llms-full.txt. Data: system.json.

## Parts
An id links to its page (import, markup, props). What it is. Use: when. Not: situation → part instead.
- [button-filled](parts/button-filled.md): The accent fill under its own words; the most prominent button. Use: It is the one action that commits a sheet, a dialog or an empty page: Save, Add category, Listen now. Not: Another filled button is on the same surface: make the second one Tonal → button-tonal.
- [button-tonal](parts/button-tonal.md): The accent container under its own words, with no outline; quieter than Filled. Use: It is the alternative beside a Filled button. Not: It is the only action that commits the surface → button-filled.
- [button-text](parts/button-text.md): An accent label with no container until it is hovered or pressed; the quietest button. Use: It dismisses, backs out or repeats: Cancel, Clear, Try again, Hide this. Not: The action must be found at a glance on its own → button-filled.
- [button-danger](parts/button-danger.md): A Text button in the danger colour. Use: It is the confirm of a delete, in a dialog that asks first: Delete, Delete source. Not: The action is not destructive, or nobody has been asked to confirm → button-text.
- [button-small](parts/button-small.md): A shorter pill, same touch target. Use: It sits in a dense row or a popover. Not: It commits a sheet → button-filled.
- [icon-btn](parts/icon-btn.md): A glyph in a round 44px target, quiet until used. Use: One glyph says what it does: Close, Back, More, Share. Not: It is the companion of a primary action: Share beside Play → icon-btn-tonal. Experimental: variant="filled".
- [icon-btn-tonal](parts/icon-btn-tonal.md): A circle on the container fill, beside a primary action. Use: The companion of a primary action in one row: Share beside Play. Not: A lone toolbar glyph, or one in every row → icon-btn.
- [fab](parts/fab.md): The page's one primary action below 64rem: a glyph and a word, floating. Use: One creating action a phone needs in reach: Catch up, Add a source. Not: The action sits in a form or a sheet → button-filled.
- [text-link](parts/text-link.md): A link inside a line of small text; the words stay inline, the target is 44px. Use: A link inside a hint, a sentence or a breadcrumb. Not: It stands alone as an action → button-text.
- [source-link](parts/source-link.md): The one link out of a story: the publisher's name, underlined on hover. Use: Name the publisher a story or a highlight came from. Not: It sits inside a sentence → text-link.
- [play-chip](parts/play-chip.md): The tonal pill that plays a briefing or one story, with its state. Use: Play an episode or a story and show idle, current, played, error or preparing. Not: A person ticks a choice → filter-chip. Experimental: primary.
- [filter-chip](parts/filter-chip.md): A checkbox drawn as a pill; ticked it takes the accent container. Use: Tick several topics or categories to include. Not: Exactly one of a few values → segmented-choice.
- [segmented-choice](parts/segmented-choice.md): One pill of radio items: pick exactly one value. Use: Choose one of two to four short values: Length, Format, Tone. Not: Switching between views → segmented-nav.
- [segmented-nav](parts/segmented-nav.md): A tonal track with one sliding pill: switch between views of the same content. Use: Switch the view of one page or panel without leaving it: a topic's Sources and Preferences. Not: Choosing the value of a setting → segmented-choice.
- [search-field](parts/search-field.md): The rounded search pill, on the container tone, with its glyph. Use: Search or filter a list by text: the Library, Sources, Downloads. Not: A text field in a form → field. Experimental: clearable.
- [icon](parts/icon.md): A filled Phosphor glyph in the colour of the text beside it. Use: A mark beside a label or alone in a button: a chevron, a plus, a check, Play. Not: The glyph must act when pressed → icon-btn. Experimental: --icon-size.
- [badge](parts/badge.md): A grey label holding one word or one number beside a name. Use: A short label names what the thing beside it is: Admin beside the wordmark. Not: The state is good, worth a look or wrong → banner.
- [switch](parts/switch.md): A track and a thumb for one setting that is on or off. Use: A setting is on or off and applies as soon as it is flipped: Sounds, Autoplay, a podcast's Enabled. Not: The choice is one of several values, or needs a Save to apply → filter-chip.
- [slider](parts/slider.md): A track with a thumb: a value between two ends, set by dragging or by the arrow keys. Use: The value is on a scale where nearby values are alike: Volume, Playback speed, a topic's weight. Not: There are two to five named options and none is between the others → filter-chip.
- [field](parts/field.md): An outlined box for text a person types: one line, or several lines (multiline). Use: A person types a short value or a few lines: a title, a feed address, a prompt. Not: The value is one of two to four short options → segmented-choice. Experimental: tonal.
- [select](parts/select.md): A native select with its own chevron. Use: A person picks one value from a list of five or more, or of names that are too long for a row of chips. Not: the value is one of two to four short options → segmented-choice.
- [menu](parts/menu.md): A short list of actions that opens from an icon button: a row each, its glyph first. Use: A card, header or row has more actions than room: Download, Add to queue, Share, Delete. Not: The person picks one value from a list → select. Experimental: flush.
- [banner](parts/banner.md): A tinted block with an icon, a title, an optional line and at most one text button. Use: A state a person must know about stays on screen: offline, a failed run, a playback error. Not: A banner in the page would be moved around by a page change (a cover between pages) → banner.
- [toast](parts/toast.md): One quiet message at a time on the inverse surface, with an optional action. Use: A brief message with Undo after a delete. Not: A notice that must stay → banner.
- [dialog](parts/dialog.md): A small centred box with a heading and a row of buttons: one question, one tap. Use: A person confirms what cannot be undone: Delete, Discard, Switch profile. Not: The question needs fields to answer → sheet.
- [sheet](parts/sheet.md): A panel over the page for a form or a list: full screen on a phone, at the right from 40rem. Use: Something to fill in or edit that needs room: New episode, a topic, a source. Not: One question and its answers → dialog.
- [drawer](parts/drawer.md): The island modal for a form: the whole screen on a phone, a panel at the right from 40rem, with Close in the header. Use: A React island opens a form over the page, as Regenerate does. Not: The sheet is drawn by Astro or a script → sheet.
- [ripple](parts/ripple.md): A wave from the touch point that fills a control's touch area, then fades. Use: A large touch target on a phone must show where it was pressed: a bottom bar tab. Not: A small control needs a press state → icon-btn.
- [btn-action-tonal](parts/btn-action-tonal.md): The one creating action in the side column (Catch up), on the action tone. Use: the Catch up action in the side column. Not: any other button → button-tonal.
- [tabs](parts/tabs.md): A sticky strip of links to the sections of one page. Use: jump to the sections of a briefing or an episode. Not: switching between two views → segmented-nav.
- [row-action](parts/row-action.md): A row that is one link or button: the whole row responds as a rounded tile. Use: a settings row that opens a sub-page. Not: a row that holds a switch or a select → settings-row.
- [card-group](parts/card-group.md): A group of rows in one rounded container on the container tone. Use: group several settings rows. Not: a single stat or number → stat-tiles.
- [settings-row](parts/settings-row.md): A row with a label and an in-place control: a switch, a select or a value. Use: a setting with a switch. Not: a row that opens another page → row-action.
- [empty-state](parts/empty-state.md): A spot illustration, a title, one line and at most two actions, for a page with nothing in it. Use: a page or section with nothing to list yet. Not: a list that has items → card-group.
- [multiselect](parts/multiselect.md): A field-like trigger that opens a list of checkable choices. Use: choose several from a long list. Not: a few choices that fit on screen → filter-chip.
- [stat-tiles](parts/stat-tiles.md): A tile per figure: the value large over its word in muted ink. Use: figures on a dashboard. Not: a list of rows → card-group.
- [section-head](parts/section-head.md): A section header with more room above than below, so it belongs to what follows. Use: title a group of rows or cards on a page.
- [meta](parts/meta.md): One quiet line of facts, separated by centered dots. Use: date, duration and source under a title.
- [cover](parts/cover.md): A generated cover image, drawn once per theme. Use: show an episode or briefing cover.

## Color roles
Components read only these (never a hex, never a primitive color).
- --color-surface: Page background.
- --color-surface-sunken: Wells, inputs, hover fills, track backgrounds.
- --color-surface-container: The tonal fill of a control that sits on the page
- --color-surface-raised: Sheets and dialogs.
- --color-surface-overlay: Floating chrome
- --color-surface-inverse: Toasts.
- --color-on-surface: The headline ink on the page and on every surface.
- --color-on-surface-reading: Running text read under a heading in on-surface
- --color-on-surface-muted: Secondary text.
- --color-on-surface-disabled: Disabled controls only.
- --color-on-surface-inverse: Text and glyphs on the inverse surface, which toasts use.
- --color-border-hairline: Decorative dividers.
- --color-border-control: Boundary of an input or segmented control.
- --color-track: Rail and scrubber track.
- --color-track-strong: Unplayed item ticks and upcoming nodes.
- --color-accent: Lingonberry.
- --color-on-accent-container: Text and icons on accent-container.
- --color-accent-container-high: The tone of an action that is not a place
- --color-on-accent-container-high: Text and icons on accent-container-high.
- --color-accent-action: The tone of the one creating action in the side column (Catch up).
- --color-on-accent-action: Text and icons on accent-action, at 4.5:1 in rest, hover and press.
- --color-on-accent: Words and glyphs on the accent fill, and a switch's thumb.
- --color-cover-accent: Defaults to the accent.
- --color-on-cover-accent: Words on a cover's accent.
- --color-focus-ring: The keyboard focus ring, in the accent.
- --color-focus-gap: Inner ring color.
- --color-scrim: Dims the page behind a sheet, dialog, drawer or picker.
- --color-on-scrim: Words on the scrim over a cover.
- --color-accent-on-inverse: The accent on the inverse surface (a toast), the other theme's step
- --color-image-outline: 1px outline on covers for perceived edge, per DESIGN.md.
- --color-success: The good state
- --color-warning: A state worth a look
- --color-danger: A failure or a destructive action.
- --color-favorite: The filled heart.
- --color-favorite-glow: The heart's halo.
- --color-info: A neutral notice tone.
- <tone>-subtle for accent, success, warning, danger, info: the tone's tinted background
- --color-<fill>-hover and -pressed for accent, accent-container, accent-container-high, accent-action, surface, surface-sunken, surface-container, surface-container-focus, surface-raised, surface-overlay, surface-inverse, surface-inverse-action, accent-subtle: its state fills

## Scales
Read directly by components.
- --space-{1 0.25rem, 2 0.5rem, 4 1rem, 6 1.5rem, 8 2rem, 12 3rem, 16 4rem, 24 6rem}
- --radius-{round 9999px}
- --shape-{xs, sm, md, lg, xl, sheet, 2xl}: corners, a style redraws them
- --stroke-{hairline 1px, rail 2px, ring 2px, ring-gap 2px}
- --duration-{press-in 100ms, press-out 160ms, hover 150ms, state 200ms, enter 250ms, exit 150ms, sheet-in 300ms, sheet-out 220ms, drawer-full 500ms, progress 250ms, stagger 40ms, theme 200ms, spin 800ms, spring-settle 650ms, spring-release 750ms, spring-pop 450ms, spring-spatial-fast 350ms, spring-spatial-default 420ms, spring-spatial-slow 570ms, spring-effects-fast 140ms, spring-effects-default 220ms, spring-effects-slow 310ms}
- --ease-{out, in-out, drawer, hover, linear linear, spring-settle, spring-release, spring-pop, spring-spatial-fast, spring-spatial-default, spring-spatial-slow, spring-effects-fast, spring-effects-default, spring-effects-slow}

## Component tokens
Sizes per part: cover, rail, item, cta, action, button, mini, player, control, scrubber, hue, segmented, field, switch, checkbox, sheet, toast, banner, archive, chip, app, queue, nav, tabs, row, slider, picker, scene, card. List one with `ds token <group>`.

---

## Filled button (`button-filled`)

The accent fill under its own words; the most prominent button.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Button`

### Markup

```astro
<Button variant="filled" type="submit">Save</Button>
```

### Use when

- It is the one action that commits a sheet, a dialog or an empty page: Save, Add category, Listen now
- It saves or submits a form sheet, or confirms a dialog

### Not when

- Another filled button is on the same surface: make the second one Tonal: use [`button-tonal`](parts/button-tonal.md)
- The action dismisses or backs out (Cancel, Hide this): use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)
- Many rows repeat it: use a Text button or an Icon button in each row: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)
- an action that only creates, in the side column: use [`btn-action-tonal`](parts/btn-action-tonal.md)

### Rules

- At most one per surface.
- Never a bold label.

### Props of Button

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"filled" \| "tonal" \| "text"` | - | Filled, tonal or text (button.ts says what each is for). |
| `tone?` | `"danger"` | - | The danger tone, for a text button that confirms a delete. |
| `size?` | `"small"` | - | Small: a shorter pill for a dense row or a popover (button.ts says when). |
| `href?` | `string` | - | Draws a link instead of a button, for an action that goes to an address. |
| `target?` | `string` | - | - |
| `rel?` | `string` | - | - |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the button where it stands (a margin, a grid area). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the button in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the button. |
| `reserve?` | `string` | - | The widest words the button may swap to ("Saving…"). It is as wide as these and its own words in every state, so a button that hugs its words never changes width when they change (DS-9). A script that swaps the words writes `[data-button-label]`, not the button, which would drop the reserve. A `reserve` button holds words only: a `.spinner` child is read as one of them and is not given the busy spinner's place (buttons.css), so give a busy button with a spinner no `reserve`. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | - |

Every attribute of a native `button` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--button-height` `--button-padding` `--button-radius` `--color-on-surface-disabled` `--color-surface` `--color-surface-container` `--cta-bg` `--cta-bg-hover` `--cta-bg-pressed` `--cta-fg`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.button-filled` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`, `styles/foundations.css`
- Files: `src/Button.tsx`, `src/button.ts`

### Owner's note

Button, filled and tonal variants (design-system/Button.tsx): the one committing action of a sheet or an empty page, and its alternative. Both fill their row.

---

## Tonal button (`button-tonal`)

The accent container under its own words, with no outline; quieter than Filled.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Button`

### Markup

```astro
<Button variant="tonal">Share</Button>
```

### Use when

- It is the alternative beside a Filled button
- It is a labelled add or reorder action on a list: Add source, Add section, Reorder

### Not when

- It is the only action that commits the surface: use [`button-filled`](parts/button-filled.md)
- It dismisses or backs out: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)

### Rules

- Matches the filled button's height.
- No outline.

### Props of Button

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"filled" \| "tonal" \| "text"` | - | Filled, tonal or text (button.ts says what each is for). |
| `tone?` | `"danger"` | - | The danger tone, for a text button that confirms a delete. |
| `size?` | `"small"` | - | Small: a shorter pill for a dense row or a popover (button.ts says when). |
| `href?` | `string` | - | Draws a link instead of a button, for an action that goes to an address. |
| `target?` | `string` | - | - |
| `rel?` | `string` | - | - |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the button where it stands (a margin, a grid area). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the button in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the button. |
| `reserve?` | `string` | - | The widest words the button may swap to ("Saving…"). It is as wide as these and its own words in every state, so a button that hugs its words never changes width when they change (DS-9). A script that swaps the words writes `[data-button-label]`, not the button, which would drop the reserve. A `reserve` button holds words only: a `.spinner` child is read as one of them and is not given the busy spinner's place (buttons.css), so give a busy button with a spinner no `reserve`. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | - |

Every attribute of a native `button` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--button-height` `--button-padding` `--button-radius` `--color-on-surface` `--color-on-surface-disabled` `--color-surface-container` `--color-surface-container-hover` `--color-surface-container-pressed`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.button-tonal` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`, `styles/foundations.css`
- Files: `src/Button.tsx`, `src/button.ts`

### Owner's note

Button, tonal variant: the mood's container tone under its own words, with no outline, as the tonal icon button and the tonal select are. Quieter than the filled button and still a button, which an outlined box on the page's own surface was not. The accent container means chosen or current alone (owner, 2026-11-04): a control at rest takes the mood's container, grey in Default and tinted in a coloured mood, so no mood needs a grey it does not have.

---

## Text button (`button-text`)

An accent label with no container until it is hovered or pressed; the quietest button.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Button`

### Markup

```astro
<Button variant="text">Cancel</Button>
```

### Use when

- It dismisses, backs out or repeats: Cancel, Clear, Try again, Hide this
- It sits beside a Filled button as the lesser choice
- It is a short action on a card or a banner: See all, Install

### Not when

- The action must be found at a glance on its own: use [`button-filled`](parts/button-filled.md)
- It has a glyph and no words: use [`icon-btn`](parts/icon-btn.md)

### Rules

- In a dialog, Cancel and the filled button sit in a DialogActions row (EpisodeActions.astro); a form sheet keeps its one filled button in `.sheet-actions`.

### Props of Button

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"filled" \| "tonal" \| "text"` | - | Filled, tonal or text (button.ts says what each is for). |
| `tone?` | `"danger"` | - | The danger tone, for a text button that confirms a delete. |
| `size?` | `"small"` | - | Small: a shorter pill for a dense row or a popover (button.ts says when). |
| `href?` | `string` | - | Draws a link instead of a button, for an action that goes to an address. |
| `target?` | `string` | - | - |
| `rel?` | `string` | - | - |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the button where it stands (a margin, a grid area). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the button in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the button. |
| `reserve?` | `string` | - | The widest words the button may swap to ("Saving…"). It is as wide as these and its own words in every state, so a button that hugs its words never changes width when they change (DS-9). A script that swaps the words writes `[data-button-label]`, not the button, which would drop the reserve. A `reserve` button holds words only: a `.spinner` child is read as one of them and is not given the busy spinner's place (buttons.css), so give a busy button with a spinner no `reserve`. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | - |

Every attribute of a native `button` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--button-radius` `--color-accent` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.button-text` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`, `styles/foundations.css`, `styles/primitives.css`
- Files: `src/Button.tsx`, `src/button.ts`

### Owner's note

Button, text variant (design-system/Button.tsx): an accent label with no container until it is hovered or pressed. Usage: Cancel, Clear, Try again; the quiet action beside or under a filled button.

---

## Danger button (`button-danger`)

A Text button in the danger colour.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Button`

### Markup

```astro
<Button variant="text" tone="danger">Delete</Button>
```

### Use when

- It is the confirm of a delete, in a dialog that asks first: Delete, Delete source

### Not when

- The action is not destructive, or nobody has been asked to confirm: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)
- It is the first control on a surface: red is for the second step, after the person has asked to delete: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)

### Props of Button

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"filled" \| "tonal" \| "text"` | - | Filled, tonal or text (button.ts says what each is for). |
| `tone?` | `"danger"` | - | The danger tone, for a text button that confirms a delete. |
| `size?` | `"small"` | - | Small: a shorter pill for a dense row or a popover (button.ts says when). |
| `href?` | `string` | - | Draws a link instead of a button, for an action that goes to an address. |
| `target?` | `string` | - | - |
| `rel?` | `string` | - | - |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the button where it stands (a margin, a grid area). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the button in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the button. |
| `reserve?` | `string` | - | The widest words the button may swap to ("Saving…"). It is as wide as these and its own words in every state, so a button that hugs its words never changes width when they change (DS-9). A script that swaps the words writes `[data-button-label]`, not the button, which would drop the reserve. A `reserve` button holds words only: a `.spinner` child is read as one of them and is not given the busy spinner's place (buttons.css), so give a busy button with a spinner no `reserve`. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | - |

Every attribute of a native `button` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--color-danger` `--color-danger-subtle` `--color-on-surface-disabled`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.button-danger` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`
- Files: `src/Button.tsx`, `src/button.ts`

### Owner's note

Button, danger tone (text variant; was .confirm-delete in episode-actions.css): red only here, once the person has asked to delete. Usage: the confirm of a delete dialog, Delete and Delete source. After the disabled rule above, which it must outrank at the same specificity.

---

## Small button (`button-small`)

A shorter pill, same touch target.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Button`

### Markup

```astro
<Button variant="text" size="small">Listen now</Button>
```

### Use when

- It sits in a dense row or a popover

### Not when

- It commits a sheet: use [`button-filled`](parts/button-filled.md)

### Props of Button

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"filled" \| "tonal" \| "text"` | - | Filled, tonal or text (button.ts says what each is for). |
| `tone?` | `"danger"` | - | The danger tone, for a text button that confirms a delete. |
| `size?` | `"small"` | - | Small: a shorter pill for a dense row or a popover (button.ts says when). |
| `href?` | `string` | - | Draws a link instead of a button, for an action that goes to an address. |
| `target?` | `string` | - | - |
| `rel?` | `string` | - | - |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the button where it stands (a margin, a grid area). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the button in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the button. |
| `reserve?` | `string` | - | The widest words the button may swap to ("Saving…"). It is as wide as these and its own words in every state, so a button that hugs its words never changes width when they change (DS-9). A script that swaps the words writes `[data-button-label]`, not the button, which would drop the reserve. A `reserve` button holds words only: a `.spinner` child is read as one of them and is not given the busy spinner's place (buttons.css), so give a busy button with a spinner no `reserve`. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | - |

Every attribute of a native `button` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--button-height-small` `--button-padding-small` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.button-small` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`
- Files: `src/Button.tsx`, `src/button.ts`

### Owner's note

Button, small size (size="small" on any variant): a shorter pill with less padding and label-size words, for a dense row or a popover where the full pill crowds the text around it (owner, 2026-11-04: Listen now in the queue). The pill is button.height-small; its target stays the touch size, as the chip's does. After the variants, so it wins at their specificity.

---

## Icon button (`icon-btn`)

A glyph in a round 44px target, quiet until used.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/IconButton`
- `@singularityfm/design-system/Icon`

### Markup

```astro
<IconButton label="Close"><Icon name="close" size="lg" /></IconButton>
```

### Use when

- One glyph says what it does: Close, Back, More, Share
- A row's dots menu, or the Close of a sheet
- A toolbar glyph, a sheet's Close, a row's dots or its end action
- Many rows repeat it

### Not when

- It is the companion of a primary action: Share beside Play: use [`icon-btn-tonal`](parts/icon-btn-tonal.md)
- The action needs a word to be understood: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)
- The action floats over the page: use [`fab`](parts/fab.md)
- A row would carry several of them: its actions go in a dots menu at its end: use [`menu`](parts/menu.md)

### Rules

- label is required: it is the button's accessible name (aria-label), as the glyph has no words.
- It draws `.press`: the press is a state layer; the glyph never scales.
- rowEnd for one that ends a row; a script or an island (a Base UI Close) takes the classes from iconButtonClass().
- A toggle sets aria-pressed and holds two glyphs, off then on (<Icon name="thumbsUp" /><Icon name="thumbsUpFill" />): the button shows the one its state calls for, and a standard one that is on takes the accent container.

### Experimental options

- `variant="filled"` (since 2026-11-12): The queue's Start listening is a Play, so it wears the primary fill with its own hover and press (owner, 2026-11-04: "every primary button one colour").

### Props of IconButton

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | - | What a press does, for a screen reader: the glyph has no words ("Close", "Share"). |
| `variant?` | `"standard" \| "tonal" \| "filled"` | `"standard"` | Standard (the default); tonal, the circle beside a primary action; or filled, a glyph that is the primary action, experimental (DS-11). iconButton.ts says when. |
| `rowEnd?` | `boolean` | `false` | It ends a row: its glyph's ink lands where the words of the rows around it end (D187). |
| `href?` | `string` | - | Draws a link instead of a button, for a glyph that goes to an address (Back). |
| `target?` | `string` | - | - |
| `rel?` | `string` | - | - |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the button where it stands, or a hook a page's rule or script finds it by. Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the button in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the button. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The glyph: an Icon, or two that the button's state swaps between. |

Every attribute of a native `button` passes through.

### Props of Icon

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `IconName` | - | - |
| `size?` | `"md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | The glyph's box: medium beside words, large when it is the whole button. |
| `className?` | `string` | `""` | A hook for the control that holds it (a rule that places the glyph, or swaps it). An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |

### Tokens it reads

`--button-radius` `--color-accent` `--color-accent-container` `--color-on-accent-container` `--color-on-surface` `--color-on-surface-disabled` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--color-surface-container` `--cta-bg` `--cta-bg-hover` `--cta-bg-pressed` `--cta-fg` `--size-icon-lg` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.icon-btn` `.press` `.icon-btn-end` `.icon-btn-filled` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`, `styles/foundations.css`
- Files: `src/IconButton.tsx`, `src/iconButton.ts`

### Owner's note

The icon button: a glyph in a round 44px target. Quiet until used; the accent is for actions that have a label.

---

Usage: add it with .icon-btn for the companion of a primary action (Share beside Play); a lone toolbar glyph stays a plain .icon-btn. Its ink is full strength, not muted, because the fill already marks it as a control.

## Floating action button (`fab`)

The page's one primary action below 64rem: a glyph and a word, floating.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Fab`

### Markup

```astro
<Fab icon="plus" label="Add source to Design">Add</Fab>
```

### Use when

- One creating action a phone needs in reach: Catch up, Add a source

### Not when

- The action sits in a form or a sheet: use [`button-filled`](parts/button-filled.md)
- From 64rem: the side column or the page carries the action as a button: use [`button-tonal`](parts/button-tonal.md)
- The action is one glyph with no word: use [`icon-btn`](parts/icon-btn.md)

### Rules

- One per page, below 64rem; from 64rem it is not shown.
- label is its whole accessible name; the word beside the glyph is hidden from a screen reader.
- A script folds it by data-folded on FAB_SELECTOR (design-system/fab.ts).

### Props of Fab

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | - | What a press does, for a screen reader, in full ("Add source to Design"). The word beside the glyph is hidden from it, so this is the button's one name. |
| `icon` | `IconName` | - | The glyph it keeps when it folds. |
| `href?` | `string` | - | Draws a link instead of a button, so the action works before any script (/create). |
| `target?` | `string` | - | - |
| `rel?` | `string` | - | - |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For a hook a page's rule or script finds it by. Never its look or its place: it floats where fab.css puts it. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the button in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the button. |
| `reserve?` | `string` | - | The widest words the button will say beside its glyph ("Resume · 88 min left"), for one whose words change. It is as wide as these in every state (DS-9); longer words end in an ellipsis. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The word the extended button shows beside its glyph ("Add"); it folds away while reading. |

Every attribute of a native `button` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--color-surface` `--cta-bg` `--cta-bg-hover` `--cta-bg-pressed` `--cta-fg` `--shape-round` `--size-icon-lg`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.create-fab` `.create-fab-label` `.add-fab` `.play-fab` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/fab.css`, `styles/foundations.css`
- Files: `src/Fab.tsx`, `src/fab.ts`

### Owner's note

The FAB (Fab.tsx): the one primary action below 64rem, as Android draws a screen's primary action (D52), where making or adding is the next thing to do. Extended, the glyph and the word, at the top of a page and while scrolling back up; folded to the glyph while scrolling down to read (the app's script sets data-folded). It carries a word, so a press shows in its fill, never by scaling it. From 64rem the side column or the page carries the same action, and this one is not shown.

---

## Text link (`text-link`)

A link inside a line of small text; the words stay inline, the target is 44px.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Link`

### Markup

```astro
<Link href="/settings">Settings</Link>
```

### Use when

- A link inside a hint, a sentence or a breadcrumb

### Not when

- It stands alone as an action: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)
- The control does something on this page: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)
- It is the one action of a surface, even one that goes to an address: use [`button-filled`](parts/button-filled.md)

### Rules

- A link is a real <a href>; an action on this page is a Button.

### Props of Link

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | `string` | - | Where it goes. A link always has an address; an action on this page is a Button. |
| `variant?` | `"text" \| "source"` | `"text"` | Text (the default), a link in a line of words, or source, a story's publisher (link.ts). |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the link where it stands, or a hook a page's rule or script finds it by. Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the link in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the link. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The words. |

### Tokens it reads

`--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.text-link` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/primitives.css`
- Files: `src/Link.tsx`, `src/link.ts`

### Owner's note

A link inside a line of small text (a settings hint): the words stay inline, the touch target is 44px tall through a hit layer centred on the line (D189 sweep, layout.spec.ts). Usage: class="text-link".

## Source link (`source-link`)

The one link out of a story: the publisher's name, underlined on hover.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Link`

### Markup

```astro
<Link variant="source" href={url} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">{publisher}</Link>
```

### Use when

- Name the publisher a story or a highlight came from

### Not when

- It sits inside a sentence: use [`text-link`](parts/text-link.md)
- The control does something on this page: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)
- It is the one action of a surface, even one that goes to an address: use [`button-filled`](parts/button-filled.md)

### Rules

- One source link everywhere, the player's included: no page draws its own copy.

### Props of Link

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | `string` | - | Where it goes. A link always has an address; an action on this page is a Button. |
| `variant?` | `"text" \| "source"` | `"text"` | Text (the default), a link in a line of words, or source, a story's publisher (link.ts). |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the link where it stands, or a hook a page's rule or script finds it by. Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the link in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the link. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The words. |

### Tokens it reads

`--button-radius` `--color-accent` `--color-accent-pressed` `--size-icon-sm` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.source-link` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/foundations.css`, `styles/primitives.css`
- Files: `src/Link.tsx`, `src/link.ts`

### Owner's note

The one link out of a story or an episode highlight: the publisher's name (or its host) and an opens-elsewhere glyph. A link, not a button: no container, no fill. On hover an underline draws in under the name from its start (a background on the span, so it animates where text-decoration does not); a press deepens the words to the pressed accent. The padding is taken back at the start, so the words sit where they would without it and the target reaches past them; at the end it stays, so the target never runs past the column.

## Play chip (`play-chip`)

The tonal pill that plays a briefing or one story, with its state.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/PlayChip`

### Markup

```astro
<PlayChip label="5 min" aria-label="Play the briefing" data-play-item={0} />
```

### Use when

- Play an episode or a story and show idle, current, played, error or preparing

### Not when

- A person ticks a choice: use [`filter-chip`](parts/filter-chip.md)
- The page's one main Play floats over it on a phone: use [`fab`](parts/fab.md)
- The action is not playing something: use [`button-tonal`](parts/button-tonal.md)

### Rules

- A native button with no client directive (DS-8): the player writes data-state, data-playing and [data-chip-label].

### Experimental options

- `primary` (since 2026-11-12): The page's one main Play (the hero's) takes the primary fill, idle and current, and shows the pause glyph while it plays, not the bars (owner, 2026-11-04: "all should have the same color synchronized"; D77). Only the fill and the glyph: its size and padding are the chip's.

### Props of PlayChip

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | - | The visible words: a length such as "1:24", or a state such as "Playing". |
| `state?` | `"idle" \| "current" \| "played" \| "preparing" \| "error" \| "unavailable"` | `"idle"` | Where the item stands; the player rewrites it (buttons.css documents each). |
| `reserve?` | `string` | `"Play again"` | The widest words the chip will ever show ("Processing"). The chip is as wide as these in every state, so nothing beside it moves when its words change; words longer than them are cut with an ellipsis. The default, "Play again", is the widest the library itself draws and covers a time, Loading, Playing, Paused and Try again. |
| `primary?` | `boolean` | `false` | The page's one main Play: the primary fill, and the pause glyph while it plays instead of the bars. Experimental (DS-11): it may change or go in a minor release (playChip.ts says why it exists). |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the chip where it stands, or a hook a page's rule finds it by. Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the chip in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the button. |

Every attribute of a native `button` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--chip-bg` `--chip-bg-current` `--chip-bg-current-hover` `--chip-bg-current-pressed` `--chip-bg-hover` `--chip-bg-pressed` `--chip-fg` `--chip-fg-current` `--chip-gap` `--chip-glyph` `--chip-height` `--chip-icon` `--chip-padding-end` `--chip-padding-start` `--chip-radius` `--color-accent-pressed` `--color-on-surface-disabled` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--color-success` `--color-surface-sunken` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.chip` `.chip-glyph` `.chip-label` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`
- Files: `src/PlayChip.tsx`, `src/playChip.ts`

### Owner's note

The tonal pill that plays a briefing or one story: a play mark and a short label on the container fill, with no outline.

## Chip (`filter-chip`)

A checkbox drawn as a pill; ticked it takes the accent container.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Chip`
- `@singularityfm/design-system/ChipGroup`

### Markup

```astro
<ChipGroup aria-label="Show"><Chip name="show" value="daily" defaultChecked>Daily</Chip></ChipGroup>
```

### Use when

- Tick several topics or categories to include
- Filter a list by one or more kinds: the Library's Show chips

### Not when

- Exactly one of a few values: use [`segmented-choice`](parts/segmented-choice.md)
- The control switches the view of the same content: use [`segmented-nav`](parts/segmented-nav.md)
- The choices are many, or long: they go in a list: use [`select`](parts/select.md)
- The pill plays a briefing or a story: use [`play-chip`](parts/play-chip.md)
- a long list of options: use [`multiselect`](parts/multiselect.md)

### Rules

- A native checkbox with no client directive (DS-8); scroll on the group for one sideways row.

### Props of Chip

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The words on the chip: the choice's name. |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the chip where it stands, or a hook a page's rule finds it by. Never its look. It goes on the chip (the label); every other attribute goes on its checkbox. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the chip in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the checkbox. |

Every attribute of a native `input` passes through.

### Props of ChipGroup

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scroll?` | `boolean` | `false` | One row that scrolls sideways when the chips do not fit, as the Library's Show chips do. |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the group where it stands (a card-group, a scroll fade), or a hook a page's rule or script finds it by. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the group in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the fieldset. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The Chips. |

### Tokens it reads

`--chip-height` `--chip-radius` `--chip-radius-selected` `--color-accent-container` `--color-accent-container-hover` `--color-accent-container-pressed` `--color-focus-ring` `--color-on-accent-container` `--color-on-surface` `--color-surface-container` `--color-surface-container-hover` `--color-surface-container-pressed` `--size-icon-sm` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.filter-chip` `.filter-chips` `.filter-chips-scroll` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/primitives.css`
- Files: `src/Chip.tsx`, `src/ChipGroup.tsx`, `src/chip.ts`

### Owner's note

The filter chip: a checkbox drawn as a pill that takes the accent container when checked, its check taking no room (D95), in a row that scrolls sideways (the Library's Show filters).

## Segmented choice (`segmented-choice`)

One pill of radio items: pick exactly one value.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/SegmentedChoice`

### Markup

```astro
<SegmentedChoice name="length" aria-label="Length" defaultValue="3" options={[{ value: "3", label: "3 min" }, { value: "5", label: "5 min" }]} />
```

### Use when

- Choose one of two to four short values: Length, Format, Tone

### Not when

- Switching between views: use [`segmented-nav`](parts/segmented-nav.md)
- Several may be ticked together: use [`filter-chip`](parts/filter-chip.md)
- The values are more than four, or long: use [`select`](parts/select.md)

### Rules

- Native radios with no client directive (DS-8).

### Props of SegmentedChoice

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | - | The radios' name, which a form posts with the chosen value. |
| `options` | `readonly SegmentedChoiceOption[]` | - | Two to four segments; any other attribute of one (data-*, disabled) goes on its radio. |
| `defaultValue?` | `string` | - | The value chosen when it is first drawn; the radios then keep their own. An Astro page's. |
| `value?` | `string` | - | The chosen value, as the state of a React island: pair it with onValueChange. |
| `onValueChange?` | `(value: string) => void` | - | - |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing it where it stands, or a hook a page's rule finds it by. Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places it in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the fieldset. |

Every attribute of a native `input` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--chip-height` `--color-accent-container` `--color-accent-container-hover` `--color-accent-container-pressed` `--color-border-control` `--color-focus-ring` `--color-on-accent-container` `--color-on-surface` `--size-icon-sm` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.segmented-choice` `.segmented-choice-item` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/primitives.css`
- Files: `src/SegmentedChoice.tsx`, `src/segmentedChoice.ts`

### Owner's note

Selection duty (2026-10-20), as Material 3's segmented button: one pill outlined with a hairline, hairline dividers between the segments, the chosen one filled with the accent container and a check before its words, the others transparent. Radios in a fieldset, so the arrow keys, the group and its name come from the browser. Told apart from .segmented-nav at a glance: an outline, not a track, and a check, not a raised pill.

## Segmented navigation (`segmented-nav`)

A tonal track with one sliding pill: switch between views of the same content.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/SegmentedNav`

### Markup

```astro
<SegmentedNav aria-label="View" tabs={[{ value: "stories", label: "Stories" }, { value: "transcript", label: "Transcript" }]} />
```

### Use when

- Switch the view of one page or panel without leaving it: a topic's Sources and Preferences

### Not when

- Choosing the value of a setting: use [`segmented-choice`](parts/segmented-choice.md)
- jumping to sections of a long page: use [`tabs`](parts/tabs.md)

### Rules

- A native tablist with no client directive (DS-8): the page calls mountSegmentedNav(list, onSelect) from design-system/segmentedNav once for each, and draws the panels (each tab's controls).

### Props of SegmentedNav

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs` | `readonly SegmentedNavTab[]` | - | Two to four views. |
| `defaultValue?` | `string` | `tabs[0]?.value` | The view chosen when it is drawn (the first by default); mountSegmentedNav() moves it after. |
| `compact?` | `boolean` | `false` | A chip's height on 44px columns, to sit in a row of chips. |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing it where it stands, or a hook a page's rule or script finds it by. Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |

### Tokens it reads

`--chip-height` `--color-accent-container` `--color-accent-container-pressed` `--color-focus-ring` `--color-on-accent-container` `--color-on-surface` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--color-surface-container` `--segmented-height` `--segmented-padding` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.segmented-nav` `.segmented-nav-tab` `.segmented-nav-compact` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/primitives.css`
- Files: `src/SegmentedNav.tsx`, `src/segmentedNav.ts`

### Owner's note

Navigation, used like tabs (2026-10-20): a tonal track with no outline and no check, and one pill in the accent container that slides under the active label, by transform alone. The design is flat, so the pill is told apart by colour, not by a shadow (2026-10-21); the choice control is told apart by its outline and check. The active label takes the pill's text colour, the others stay muted. Buttons in a tablist: segmentedNav.ts moves aria-selected and the roving tabindex, and answers Left, Right, Home and End.

---

## Search field (`search-field`)

The rounded search pill, on the container tone, with its glyph.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/SearchField`

### Markup

```astro
<SearchField label="Search your library" name="q" placeholder="Search your library" />
```

### Use when

- Search or filter a list by text: the Library, Sources, Downloads

### Not when

- A text field in a form: use [`field`](parts/field.md)
- A person picks one of a known list: use [`select`](parts/select.md)

### Rules

- A native input with no client directive (DS-8).
- clearable draws a Clear text button at its end; the page calls installSearchClear() (design-system/searchField) on each page load, and syncSearchClear(input) after it sets the text itself.

### Experimental options

- `clearable` (since 2026-11-12): A Clear text button in the field (owner, 2026-10-08, ledger reading-library.md): the native one differs in every browser and is hidden, and without room for the button the typed text runs under it. On the Library, the Sources filter, Blocked outlets, Downloads and the emoji search.

### Props of SearchField

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | - | The input's name for a screen reader ("Search your library"); the glyph and the hint show it. |
| `clearable?` | `boolean` | `false` | A Clear text button at the field's end, shown while it holds text. The page calls installSearchClear() from design-system/searchField once per page load. Experimental (DS-11): it may change or go in a minor release (searchField.ts says why it exists). |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the field where it stands, or a hook a page's rule finds it by. Never its look. It goes on the outer element (the pill, or the wrapper of a clearable field); every other attribute goes on its input. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the field in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the input. |

Every attribute of a native `input` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--color-border-control` `--color-on-surface` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--color-surface-container` `--color-surface-container-focus` `--color-surface-container-hover` `--field-height` `--shape-round` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.search-field` `.search-field-wrap` `.search-field-clear` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`, `styles/search-field.css`
- Files: `src/SearchField.tsx`, `src/searchField.ts`

### Owner's note

The search field: a filled pill with the glyph inside it, as a search bar is in every Google app. The glyph and the placeholder say what it is. Focus lifts it (the overlay fill and a hairline; the design is flat, so no shadow); the ring is the keyboard's only (data-input, app.ts), so a tap, a click or typing never draws it. It is keyed off the pointer, not on the keyboard, so a page with no input script still shows keyboard users their place (2026-11-10). Library, Sources and every topic's page share this one field (2026-10-21; styles.test.ts holds them to it).

---

## Icon (`icon`)

A filled Phosphor glyph in the colour of the text beside it.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Icon`

### Markup

```astro
<Icon name="plus" size="lg" />
```

### Use when

- A mark beside a label or alone in a button: a chevron, a plus, a check, Play

### Not when

- The glyph must act when pressed: use [`icon-btn`](parts/icon-btn.md)
- the glyph must act when pressed: use [`icon-btn`](parts/icon-btn.md)

### Rules

- Draw it with <Icon>; a script builds one with iconHtml() and an island with <Icon> from player/ui, both through iconClass().
- A control that holds a glyph and needs another size sets --icon-size on itself (experimental), never a rule on the glyph.
- A chevron in an icon button or a field with aria-haspopup turns as aria-expanded turns true; it needs no rule of its own.

### Experimental options

- `--icon-size` (since 2026-11-12): A control that holds a glyph sets its size once, on itself, so no page rule names the glyph: the transport's Play larger than everything around it and its skips (2026-10-22), the cover's bare Play on the scrim (owner, 2026-10-31), the Library's status mark sized from its text (owner, 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-03), and the queue ring's end check in the ring's own size (owner, 2026-11-12: keep it as it is).

### Props of Icon

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `IconName` | - | - |
| `size?` | `"md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | The glyph's box: medium beside words, large when it is the whole button. |
| `className?` | `string` | `""` | A hook for the control that holds it (a rule that places the glyph, or swaps it). An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |

### Tokens it reads

`--color-favorite` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--icon-bold` `--size-icon` `--size-icon-lg`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.icon-glyph` `.icon-glyph-lg` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/icon.css`
- Files: `src/Icon.tsx`, `src/icon.ts`

### Owner's note

Phosphor: every glyph is one filled path, so an icon is just its colour and its size. --icon-size, experimental (DS-11, 2026-11-12): a control that holds a glyph sets its size once, on itself, so no page rule names the glyph (the transport's Play and skips, the cover's Play, the Library's status mark, the queue ring's end check: owner calls of 2026-10-22, 2026-10-31, 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-03, and 2026-11-12 for the ring). It inherits, so it is set on the control that holds the one glyph, never on a container of several controls. The registry lists it (icon.ts, ICON.experimental).

## Badge (`badge`)

A grey label holding one word or one number beside a name.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Badge`

### Markup

```astro
<Badge>Admin</Badge>
```

### Use when

- A short label names what the thing beside it is: Admin beside the wordmark
- A count of what a section holds

### Not when

- The state is good, worth a look or wrong: use [`banner`](parts/banner.md)
- The pill can be pressed or ticked: use [`filter-chip`](parts/filter-chip.md)
- the pill can be pressed or ticked: use [`filter-chip`](parts/filter-chip.md)

### Rules

- It holds one word or one number; the page places it with a class, never styles it.

### Props of Badge

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className?` | `string` | `""` | For placing the badge where it stands (a margin, a grid area). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | The one word or one number it holds. |

### Tokens it reads

`--color-on-surface-muted` `--color-surface-container`

### Where it is drawn

- Styled in: `styles/badge.css`
- Files: `src/Badge.tsx`, `src/badge.ts`

### Owner's note

The Badge (design-system/Badge.tsx): a grey pill that holds one word or one number. One size, one fill. It is as wide as its words and no narrower than it is high, so a single digit stays round. Grey, so the blue stays with the controls (owner, 2026-10-30).

## Switch (`switch`)

A track and a thumb for one setting that is on or off.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Switch`

### Markup

```astro
<div class="settings-row"><label class="settings-label" for="autoplay">Autoplay</label><Switch id="autoplay" name="autoplay" /></div>
```

### Use when

- A setting is on or off and applies as soon as it is flipped: Sounds, Autoplay, a podcast's Enabled
- It sits at the end of a settings row, with the row's label as its name
- One switch stands for a group of switches (a master): the script sets `indeterminate` on it, and unchecks it, while only some of the group are on. The track sits halfway between the off grey and the accent and the thumb halfway along it. Pressing it turns the whole group on, or off when all are on

### Not when

- The choice is one of several values, or needs a Save to apply: use [`filter-chip`](parts/filter-chip.md)
- The control starts an action (Catch up, Delete) and has no state of its own: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)
- Several options may be ticked together in a list: use [`filter-chip`](parts/filter-chip.md)

### Rules

- It is the native checkbox (role="switch") and takes no client directive (DS-8): an Astro page starts it with defaultChecked, a React island passes checked with onChange.

### Props of Switch

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the switch where it stands (a margin, a grid area). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `style?` | `CSSProperties \| string` | - | Inline style, as an object or the string an Astro page writes; never its look. |

Every attribute of a native `input` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--color-accent` `--color-accent-hover` `--color-accent-pressed` `--color-border-control` `--color-on-accent` `--size-touch` `--switch-height` `--switch-padding` `--switch-radius` `--switch-thumb` `--switch-thumb-bg` `--switch-thumb-radius` `--switch-track-hover` `--switch-track-mixed` `--switch-width`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.switch-input` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/switch.css`
- Files: `src/Switch.tsx`, `src/switch.ts`

### Owner's note

One setting that is on or off, a checkbox with role="switch" drawn as a track; its ::before is the thumb.

---

## Slider (`slider`)

A track with a thumb: a value between two ends, set by dragging or by the arrow keys.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Slider`

### Markup

```astro
<Slider aria-label="Volume" min={0} max={1} step={0.05} defaultValue={0.7} style="--range-fill: 70%" />
```

### Use when

- The value is on a scale where nearby values are alike: Volume, Playback speed, a topic's weight

### Not when

- There are two to five named options and none is between the others: use [`filter-chip`](parts/filter-chip.md)
- Only on and off are possible: use [`switch`](parts/switch.md)

### Rules

- It is the native range and takes no client directive (DS-8): an Astro page starts it with defaultValue, a React island passes value with onChange.
- WebKit paints the filled track from --range-fill, which starts at 0%: set it to (value - min) / (max - min) as a percentage and update it on input.

### Props of Slider

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the slider where it stands (a width, a flex basis). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `style?` | `CSSProperties \| string` | - | Inline style, as an object or the string an Astro page writes; never its look. |
| `hue?` | `boolean` | `false` | A hue: the rail is the whole spectrum, the thumb is the colour picked, and a swatch floats above it while it is held (D328). The caller keeps --range-fill on the field the slider is wrapped in. |
| `wavy?` | `boolean` | `false` | The track up to the thumb drifts (a wave in Expressive, a zigzag in Halloween) and the rest stays straight; Default draws the plain Slider. The caller keeps --range-fill on the field the input is wrapped in. |

Every attribute of a native `input` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--button-radius` `--color-accent` `--color-accent-hover` `--color-accent-pressed` `--color-border-control` `--color-surface` `--scrubber-thumb` `--scrubber-thumb-active-scale` `--scrubber-thumb-ring` `--scrubber-track` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.slider-input` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/slider.css`
- Files: `src/Slider.tsx`, `src/slider.ts`

### Owner's note

A value between two ends, set by dragging a thumb or with the arrow keys. A native range. WebKit has no pseudo-element for the filled part of the track, so the track paints it as a gradient up to --range-fill, which the script keeps at (value - min) / (max - min) as a percentage. Firefox has ::-moz-range-progress and ignores the gradient. The two engines' pseudo-elements cannot share a rule: a selector one engine does not know drops the whole rule in the other.

---

## Field (`field`)

An outlined box for text a person types: one line, or several lines (multiline).

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Field`

### Markup

```astro
<div class="manage-field"><label for="title">Title</label><Field id="title" name="title" type="text" /></div>
```

### Use when

- A person types a short value or a few lines: a title, a feed address, a prompt
- It sits under its own label in a form or a settings row

### Not when

- The value is one of two to four short options: use [`segmented-choice`](parts/segmented-choice.md)
- A person picks one value from a list: use [`select`](parts/select.md)
- The setting is on or off and applies as soon as it is flipped: use [`switch`](parts/switch.md)
- The value is a number on a scale: use [`slider`](parts/slider.md)

### Rules

- It needs no client directive: it is a native input, and types and submits before any script (DS-8).
- Draw it with <Field> (multiline for a textarea); a select or a script takes the class from fieldClass().
- A disabled field dims like a disabled switch; a disabled fieldset dims it the same way, on the same element.
- A readonly field draws itself sunken, in quieter ink: no page rule.

### Experimental options

- `tonal` (since 2026-11-12): The Topics panel's fields are tonal, as its selects and chips are (owner, 2026-10-21: "one style now"); on a card a text field takes the page's surface (owner, 2026-10-24). An outlined Select there passes data-tonal on to its select.

### Props of Field

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `multiline?` | `boolean` | `false` | Several lines that grow with the text; the corner arc is a pill's, shortened. |
| `maxLines?` | `number` | - | How many lines a multiline field grows to before it scrolls inside; 6 when left out. |
| `tonal?` | `boolean` | `false` | The container's fill and no outline, for a form whose selects are tonal too (it writes data-tonal; an outlined Select there takes data-tonal itself). Experimental (DS-11): it may change or go in a minor release (field.ts says why it exists). |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the field where it stands (a width, a margin). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |

Every attribute of a native `input` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--button-radius` `--color-accent` `--color-border-hairline` `--color-danger` `--color-on-surface` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--color-surface-container` `--color-surface-container-hover` `--color-surface-container-pressed` `--color-surface-sunken` `--field-border` `--field-chevron-gap` `--field-height` `--field-padding` `--field-radius` `--field-radius-multiline` `--size-icon`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.field-input` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/field.css`
- Files: `src/Field.tsx`, `src/field.ts`

### Owner's note

The text field, and the select and textarea that share its looks: a filled pill (D186; a textarea 24px), the one control with an outline, which shows on focus.

---

## Select (`select`)

A native select with its own chevron.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Select`

### Markup

```astro
<Select variant="tonal" label="Sort" data-library-sort><option value="newest">Newest first</option></Select>
```

### Use when

- A person picks one value from a list of five or more, or of names that are too long for a row of chips
- It sits under its own label in a form, or in a toolbar as a sort or a filter

### Not when

- the value is one of two to four short options: use [`segmented-choice`](parts/segmented-choice.md)
- several values may be ticked together: use [`multiselect`](parts/multiselect.md)

### Rules

- A native select with no client directive (DS-8); a page that draws one calls installSelectSheet() once for the phone's sheet.
- Outlined (the default) is a value in a form; tonal is a sort or a filter and takes data-active on its wrapper (find it with closest("[data-select]")) once its value is not the default.
- A select inside a settings row takes class="value-select" from settings.css, which draws it as the row's value.
- data-wheel on a short ordered run (the hours of a day) opens its phone sheet as a Wheel (design-system/wheel.ts), not as rows.

### Props of Select

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant?` | `"outlined" \| "tonal"` | `"outlined"` | Outlined for a value in a form, tonal for a sort or a filter (select.ts says which is which). |
| `label?` | `string` | - | A name for a select that has no label of its own; read aloud, never drawn. Draws a label around it. |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the select where it stands (a width, a margin). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `reserve?` | `string` | - | A tonal select's longest option text ("Longest first"); an outlined select ignores it. Where the browser draws the closed select as its chosen option (appearance: base-select) it is as wide as that option, so it grows and shrinks as a person picks. With a reserve it is as wide as these words in every state (DS-9). |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | The options: `<option>` and `<optgroup>`, as a native select holds them. |

### Tokens it reads

`--button-radius` `--chip-height` `--color-accent` `--color-accent-container` `--color-accent-container-hover` `--color-border-hairline` `--color-focus-ring` `--color-on-accent-container` `--color-on-surface` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--color-surface-container` `--color-surface-container-hover` `--color-surface-container-pressed` `--color-surface-overlay` `--color-surface-overlay-hover` `--color-surface-overlay-pressed` `--field-chevron-gap` `--shadow-popover` `--shape-2xl` `--size-icon` `--size-icon-sm` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.select-outlined` `.select-tonal` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/select.css`
- Files: `src/Select.tsx`, `src/select.ts`, `src/selectSheet.ts`, `src/wheel.ts`

### Owner's note

The box and its text are the Field's (field.css, select.field-input); the wrapper holds the chevron a select draws for itself, in the muted ink, never taking a press.

## Menu (`menu`)

A short list of actions that opens from an icon button: a row each, its glyph first.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Menu`
- `@singularityfm/design-system/MenuItem`
- `@singularityfm/design-system/Icon`

### Markup

```astro
<Menu id="row-menu-3" title="Daily"><MenuItem><Icon name="pencilSimple" />Edit</MenuItem><MenuItem tone="danger"><Icon name="trash" />Delete</MenuItem></Menu>
```

### Use when

- A card, header or row has more actions than room: Download, Add to queue, Share, Delete
- Each action is one tap, with no choice of its own
- It has five actions or more: on a phone's sheet the first three become a row of tiles above the rest (menuHasTiles). Fewer than five are all rows

### Not when

- The person picks one value from a list: use [`select`](parts/select.md)
- The only action is the one the button names: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)

### Rules

- A native popover with no client directive: its button opens it with popoverTarget (DS-8).
- Under 40rem a menu is a sheet, never a small popover.
- A script finds one with MENU_SELECTORS (design-system/menu.ts); a string builder or an island takes menuListClass() and menuItemClass().

### Experimental options

- `flush` (since 2026-11-12): A host that draws its own header and body in the menu's surface (the queue's popover, the emoji picker) keeps them flush with its edges, with no list padding above and below (owner, 2026-11-12: keep the queue popover and emoji picker as they are).

### Props of Menu

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | - | The popover's id: the button that opens it names it with popoverTarget. |
| `title` | `string` | - | The sheet's header on a phone, and the menu's name for a screen reader. |
| `subtitle?` | `string` | - | A quiet line under the title on a phone's sheet, such as a card's facts. |
| `flush?` | `boolean` | - | No padding above and below the list, for a host that draws its own header and body in the menu's surface. Experimental (DS-11): it may change or go in a minor release (menu.ts says why it exists). |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the popover under its own button (the anchor of a row or a story). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | The rows: MenuItem, and a tiles row of them. |

### Props of MenuItem

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone?` | `"danger"` | - | The danger tone, for the one row that destroys. |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the row where it stands, or a hook a script finds it by. Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the row in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the row. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | The row's glyph first, then its words. |

Every attribute of a native `button` passes through.

### Props of Icon

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `IconName` | - | - |
| `size?` | `"md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | The glyph's box: medium beside words, large when it is the whole button. |
| `className?` | `string` | `""` | A hook for the control that holds it (a rule that places the glyph, or swaps it). An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |

### Tokens it reads

`--color-accent` `--color-accent-container` `--color-accent-container-hover` `--color-accent-container-pressed` `--color-border-hairline` `--color-danger` `--color-on-accent-container` `--color-on-surface` `--color-on-surface-disabled` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--color-scrim` `--color-surface-overlay` `--color-surface-overlay-hover` `--color-surface-overlay-pressed` `--layout-column` `--shadow-popover` `--shape-2xl` `--shape-md` `--shape-sheet` `--shape-xl` `--sheet-bg` `--sheet-bg-hover` `--sheet-bg-pressed` `--sheet-shadow` `--sheet-tile-bg` `--sheet-tile-bg-hover` `--sheet-tile-bg-pressed` `--size-icon` `--size-option` `--size-touch`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.menu-list` `.menu-sheet` `.menu-item` `.menu-item-danger` `.menu-tiles` `.menu-tile` `.menu-item-value` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`, `styles/menu.css`
- Files: `src/Menu.tsx`, `src/MenuItem.tsx`, `src/menu.ts`

### Owner's note

A popover lives in the top layer, so it is placed against the viewport, not the row. Where anchor positioning exists it hangs under the button, right edges level; elsewhere heroMenu.ts writes --menu-top and --menu-right from the button's box when it opens.
