## Banner (`banner`)

A tinted block with an icon, a title, an optional line and at most one text button.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Banner`

### Markup

```astro
<Banner tone="danger" icon="alert" title="Download failed" />
```

### Use when

- A state a person must know about stays on screen: offline, a failed run, a playback error

### Not when

- A banner in the page would be moved around by a page change (a cover between pages): use [`banner`](parts/banner.md)
- a message that clears itself: use [`toast`](parts/toast.md)
- a page with nothing to list: use [`empty-state`](parts/empty-state.md)

### Rules

- Only the icon takes the tone.
- An island draws one with bannerClass() and bannerText.

### Props of Banner

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `"warning" \| "danger" \| "success"` | - | - |
| `variant?` | `"block" \| "strip"` | - | "strip" is a band across the width for a state of the device; the place that holds it makes room for it. |
| `icon` | `IconName` | - | - |
| `iconFrom?` | `IconName` | - | A strip only: the glyph the icon is drawn over and strikes through (Wi-Fi, then Offline). |
| `title` | `string` | - | - |
| `body?` | `string` | - | - |
| `bodyId?` | `string` | - | An id for the body line (the title when there is none), so a control the banner explains can point at it (aria-describedby). |
| `action?` | `{ label: string; href: string }` | - | One way on, as a text button. A link, so it works for any reader and without script. |

### Tokens it reads

`--banner-padding` `--banner-radius` `--banner-strip-danger` `--banner-strip-success` `--banner-strip-warning` `--color-danger` `--color-danger-subtle` `--color-success` `--color-success-subtle` `--color-warning` `--color-warning-subtle` `--size-icon`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.banner-notice` `.banner-text` `.banner-title` `.banner-body` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/banner.css`
- Files: `src/Banner.tsx`, `src/banner.ts`

### Owner's note

Banners, and the pages with nothing to list. A banner is flat: a tinted ground, an icon in the tone's colour, a title, a line of text and at most one text button. The tone sets the tint.

---

## Toast (`toast`)

One quiet message at a time on the inverse surface, with an optional action.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Toast`
- `@singularityfm/design-system/toastStore`

### Markup

```astro
showToast({ message: "Deleted", actionLabel: "Undo", onAction })
```

### Use when

- A brief message with Undo after a delete
- A failure, which stays until it is closed or retried, or a partial save
- A run that finished while its sheet was closed

### Not when

- A notice that must stay: use [`banner`](parts/banner.md)
- A person must decide before going on: use [`dialog`](parts/dialog.md)

### Rules

- Mount <Toast client:idle /> once per page; call showToast() from toastStore, or sendToast() from toastEvent in code that must not load the store.
- The page says where it sits with --toast-nav, --toast-dock, --toast-lift and --toast-inline-start/-end on the root, never with a rule on .toast.

### Props of Toast

No props of its own.

### Tokens it reads

`--color-accent-on-inverse` `--color-surface-inverse` `--color-surface-inverse-action-hover` `--color-surface-inverse-action-pressed` `--color-surface-inverse-hover` `--color-surface-inverse-pressed` `--layout-dialog` `--shape-md` `--shape-round` `--size-touch` `--toast-bg` `--toast-fg`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.toast` `.toast-action` `.toast-dismiss` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`, `styles/toast.css`
- Files: `src/Toast.tsx`, `src/toast.ts`, `src/toastStore.ts`, `src/toastEvent.ts`

### Owner's note

The Toast (Toast.tsx). One quiet message at a time: a flat, inverse surface with a hairline radius, an optional leading icon (a check or an alert, so the outcome is not told by colour alone), the message at the label size, at most one text action in the accent and a close button, shown only to a mouse (below). A top-layer popover above whatever is docked at the bottom. Where it sits is the page's to say, by custom properties set on the root (never on .toast, so the component's rules stay the only ones that draw it): --toast-nav the navigation bar at the bottom; else --bottom-nav-height, else the safe area --toast-dock a docked bar above the navigation (the reader's mini player); 0 by default --toast-lift more room under it (the reader's run line); 0 by default --toast-inline-start the start inset it centres from; else --side-nav-width, else 0 --toast-inline-end the end inset; 0 by default

---

## Dialog (`dialog`)

A small centred box with a heading and a row of buttons: one question, one tap.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Dialog`
- `@singularityfm/design-system/DialogActions`
- `@singularityfm/design-system/DialogTitle`
- `@singularityfm/design-system/Button`

### Markup

```astro
<Dialog aria-labelledby="t"><DialogTitle id="t">Delete?</DialogTitle><DialogActions><Button variant="text">Cancel</Button></DialogActions></Dialog>
```

### Use when

- A person confirms what cannot be undone: Delete, Discard, Switch profile

### Not when

- The question needs fields to answer: use [`sheet`](parts/sheet.md)
- a form that slides in, with fields: use [`sheet`](parts/sheet.md)

### Rules

- A script finds one with DIALOG_SELECTOR; one it builds uses dialogClass(), dialogBodyClass() and dialogActionsClass().
- It renders closed, with no client directive: a script opens it with dialog.showModal() (an island through ref) and closes it with dialog.close() from the Cancel button's click.

### Props of Dialog

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form?` | `Record<string, unknown>` | - | Attributes for a form body: the dialog then submits. Without it the body is a plain box. An Astro page writes them as HTML does (`novalidate`, `method: "dialog"`). |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the dialog where it stands. Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | The question, its words and its DialogActions, inside the body. |
| `after?` | `ReactNode` | - | What sits after the body, outside the form: a hidden part a script reads (data-copy). |

Every attribute of a native `dialog` passes through.

### Props of DialogActions

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stacked?` | `boolean` | `false` | Three answers in a column, the committing one first. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | The answers: Buttons, Cancel first in a row. |

### Props of DialogTitle

No props of its own.

### Props of Button

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"filled" \| "tonal" \| "text"` | - | Filled, tonal or text (button.ts says what each is for). |
| `tone?` | `"danger"` | - | The danger tone, for a text button that confirms a delete. |
| `size?` | `"small"` | - | Small: a shorter pill for a dense row or a popover (button.ts says when). |
| `href?` | `string` | - | Draws a link instead of a button, for an action that goes to an address. |
| `target?` | `string` | - | - |
| `rel?` | `string` | - | - |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the button where it stands (a margin, a grid area). Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the button in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the button. |
| `reserve?` | `string` | - | The widest words the button may swap to ("Saving…"). It is as wide as these and its own words in every state, so a button that hugs its words never changes width when they change (DS-9). A script that swaps the words writes `[data-button-label]`, not the button, which would drop the reserve. A `reserve` button holds words only: a `.spinner` child is read as one of them and is not given the busy spinner's place (buttons.css), so give a busy button with a spinner no `reserve`. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | - |

Every attribute of a native `button` passes through.

### Tokens it reads

`--color-on-surface` `--color-scrim` `--shape-lg` `--sheet-bg` `--sheet-shadow`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.dialog-panel` `.dialog-body` `.dialog-actions` `.dialog-actions-stacked` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`, `styles/dialog.css`
- Files: `src/Dialog.tsx`, `src/DialogActions.tsx`, `src/DialogTitle.tsx`, `src/dialog.ts`

---

## Sheet (`sheet`)

A panel over the page for a form or a list: full screen on a phone, at the right from 40rem.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Sheet`
- `@singularityfm/design-system/SheetHeader`

### Markup

```astro
<Sheet title="Regenerate" titleId="regen-title" close="data-dialog-close"><form>...</form></Sheet>
```

### Use when

- Something to fill in or edit that needs room: New episode, a topic, a source
- A list over the page, dismissed by a pull or tap

### Not when

- One question and its answers: use [`dialog`](parts/dialog.md)
- A short list of actions: use [`menu`](parts/menu.md)
- A form in a Base UI island: use [`drawer`](parts/drawer.md)

### Rules

- A native dialog with no client directive: a script finds one with SHEET_SELECTOR (design-system/sheet.ts) and opens it with showModal(); kind="create" is the New episode sheet, every other is a "panel".
- A header a script builds is sheetHeadHtml() (design-system/sheetHead.ts); never write the row or its Close by hand.
- `sheet-field*`, `sheet-form` and `sheet-actions` are form layout in sheets.css, not the shell.

### Props of Sheet

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | - | The sheet's name: an h2 whose id the dialog's aria-labelledby names. |
| `titleId` | `string` | - | - |
| `close` | `"data-create-close" \| "data-panel-close" \| "data-dialog-close" \| "data-menu-close"` | - | The data attribute the sheet's script finds its Close button by. |
| `titleData?` | `` Record<`data-${string}`, string \| boolean> `` | - | Any data attribute the title carries for its script, such as data-panel-title. |
| `kind?` | `"create" \| "panel"` | `"panel"` | "create" is the New episode sheet; every other sheet is a "panel". |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the sheet where it stands. Never its look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | The form or list, inside the scrolling body. |
| `after?` | `ReactNode` | - | What sits after the body, outside its scroll: a sticky foot, a hidden part a script reads. |

Every attribute of a native `dialog` passes through.

### Props of SheetHeader

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | - | The sheet's name: an h2 whose id the dialog's aria-labelledby names. |
| `titleId` | `string` | - | - |
| `close` | `"data-create-close" \| "data-panel-close" \| "data-dialog-close" \| "data-menu-close"` | - | The data attribute the sheet's script finds its Close button by. |
| `titleData?` | `` Record<`data-${string}`, string \| boolean> `` | `{}` | Any data attribute the title carries for its script, such as data-panel-title. |
| `subtitle?` | `string` | - | A quiet line under the title: what the sheet is about, as a menu's item facts. |

### Tokens it reads

`--app-bar-height` `--button-height` `--color-border-hairline` `--color-on-surface` `--color-scrim` `--color-surface` `--color-surface-container` `--color-surface-hover` `--color-surface-pressed` `--shape-sheet` `--sheet-bg` `--sheet-bg-hover` `--sheet-bg-pressed` `--sheet-shadow`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.sheet-side` `.sheet-head` `.sheet-body` `.sheet-title` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/sheet.css`
- Files: `src/Sheet.tsx`, `src/sheet.ts`, `src/SheetHeader.tsx`, `src/sheetHead.ts`

---

## Drawer (`drawer`)

The island modal for a form: the whole screen on a phone, a panel at the right from 40rem, with Close in the header.

### Markup

```astro
<SheetFrame open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Create" closeLabel="Close">...</SheetFrame>
```

### Use when

- A React island opens a form over the page, as Regenerate does

### Not when

- The sheet is drawn by Astro or a script: use [`sheet`](parts/sheet.md)
- One question and its answers: use [`dialog`](parts/dialog.md)

### Rules

- Mount SheetFrame; it draws the scrim, viewport, popup and panel from drawer.ts, and the Sheet's head.
- Motion uses --duration-sheet-in, --duration-sheet-out and --ease-drawer.

### Tokens it reads

`--color-on-surface` `--color-scrim` `--color-surface` `--color-surface-hover` `--color-surface-pressed` `--shape-sheet` `--sheet-bg` `--sheet-bg-hover` `--sheet-bg-pressed` `--sheet-shadow` `--sheet-tile-bg` `--sheet-tile-bg-hover` `--sheet-tile-bg-pressed`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.drawer-scrim` `.drawer-viewport` `.drawer-popup` `.drawer-panel` (drawn by the app's own component the markup names; this package does not ship it yet)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`, `styles/drawer.css`, `styles/foundations.css`
- Files: `src/drawer.ts`

### Owner's note

The Drawer's surface: a scrim over the page that fades as the sheet is swiped away, a viewport, and the popup that rests on the screen's edge.

---

## Ripple (`ripple`)

A wave from the touch point that fills a control's touch area, then fades.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Ripple`

### Markup

```astro
<a href="/library" data-ripple><Ripple />Library</a>
```

### Use when

- A large touch target on a phone must show where it was pressed: a bottom bar tab

### Not when

- A small control needs a press state: use [`icon-btn`](parts/icon-btn.md)

### Rules

- The control is `position: relative` with its own stacking context (isolation: isolate); the layer sits beneath its icon and label.
- To reach past the control's box set --ripple-reach-start, --ripple-reach-end or --ripple-reach-bottom on the control; --ripple-display: none turns the layer off where the control has a pointer state.
- installRipple() (design-system/ripple.ts) is called once by the app script; the control sets nothing else.

### Props of Ripple

No props of its own.

### Tokens it reads

`--color-on-surface`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.ripple-area` `.ripple-wave` (a page draws the component, never types these)
- Styled in: `styles/ripple.css`
- Files: `src/Ripple.tsx`, `src/ripple.ts`

---

## Tonal action (`btn-action-tonal`)

The one creating action in the side column (Catch up), on the action tone.

### Use when

- the Catch up action in the side column

### Not when

- any other button: use [`button-tonal`](parts/button-tonal.md)

### Tokens it reads

`--action-tonal-radius` `--color-surface` `--cta-bg` `--cta-bg-hover` `--cta-bg-pressed` `--cta-fg`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.btn-action-tonal` (typed on your own element)
- Styled in: `styles/buttons.css`

### Owner's note

Tonal action: the one creating action in the side column (Catch up, AppNav.astro). Usage: add it to the action's own element, which keeps its size and layout. It wears the primary fill, the filled button's and Play's (owner, 2026-11-04: "all should have the same color synchronized"); it was a third, saturated tone of its own (owner, 2026-10-27), which read as a second primary beside Play. The current row's accent container still means "you are here" alone. - A 16px rounded rectangle: the one recorded exception to the pill rule (D186), so its shape alone tells it from the pill-shaped current row beside it (--action-tonal-radius). - Flat: no elevation and no shadow (owner, 2026-10-27). - Hover and press take the primary fill's own steps (--cta-bg-hover, --cta-bg-pressed).

A sticky strip of links to the sections of one page.

- jump to the sections of a briefing or an episode
- tabs inside a card

### Not when

### Rules

- Drawn only for two sections or more.

### Props of SectionTabs

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sections` | `readonly SectionRef[]` | - | - |

### Tokens it reads

`--color-accent` `--color-accent-pressed` `--color-border-hairline` `--color-on-surface` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--color-surface` `--row-radius` `--tabs-height` `--tabs-indicator-height` `--tabs-indicator-radius`

### Where it is drawn

- Styled in: `styles/primitives.css`
- Files: `src/SectionTabs.tsx`

### Owner's note

The bar sticks and carries the surface and the line under it; the strip inside it scrolls and fades its ends. A mask on the bar itself would fade its surface and line too, and what scrolls under a stuck strip would show through at its edges.

## Row action (`row-action`)

A row that is one link or button: the whole row responds as a rounded tile.

### Import

- `@singularityfm/design-system/Icon`

### Markup

```astro
<a class="row-action" href="/settings/schedule"><span class="settings-text"><span class="settings-label">Daily</span><span class="settings-hint">Every other day</span></span><Icon name="chevronRight" /></a>
```

### Use when

- a settings row that opens a sub-page
- a menu or list row that navigates
- a row with a label, a hint and a chevron

### Not when

- a row that holds a switch or a select: use [`settings-row`](parts/settings-row.md)
- a destructive or non-navigating action: use [`button-text`](parts/button-text.md)

### Rules

- Label in regular weight, never bold.
- Sits in a `.rows.card-group`.

### Props of Icon

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `IconName` | - | - |
| `size?` | `"md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | The glyph's box: medium beside words, large when it is the whole button. |
| `className?` | `string` | `""` | A hook for the control that holds it (a rule that places the glyph, or swaps it). An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |

### Tokens it reads

`--color-focus-ring` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--row-tile-radius` `--size-touch-comfortable`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.row-action` `.settings-text` `.settings-label` `.settings-hint` (typed on your own element)
- Styled in: `styles/foundations.css`, `styles/primitives.css`, `styles/settings-rows.css`

### Owner's note

A row that is one link or button: the whole row responds. Its fill is a rounded tile clear of the hairlines and reaching a little past the words, as a menu's options are, so a hovered row reads as one thing to press rather than a band across the page.

---

## Card group (`card-group`)

A group of rows in one rounded container on the container tone.

### Use when

- group several settings rows
- a card of chips
- one note that is an offer, with the accent tone

### Not when

- a single stat or number: use [`stat-tiles`](parts/stat-tiles.md)

### Rules

- A card of one row follows its height for its corner.
- Dividers run edge to edge inside.

### Tokens it reads

`--card-chip-hover` `--card-inner-radius` `--card-inset` `--card-padding` `--card-radius` `--color-border-hairline` `--color-on-surface` `--color-surface` `--color-surface-container` `--color-surface-container-hover` `--color-surface-container-pressed` `--color-surface-hover` `--color-surface-overlay` `--color-surface-overlay-hover` `--color-surface-overlay-pressed` `--row-padding-block` `--shape-xl`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.card-group` `.rows` (typed on your own element)
- Styled in: `styles/field.css`, `styles/primitives.css`, `styles/search-field.css`, `styles/select.css`, `styles/settings-rows.css`

### Owner's note

A group of settings rows in one rounded container on the container tone, as Material 3 groups an Android settings screen: the group is told apart from the page by tone alone, never by a shadow or a line. Put the class on the .rows list itself; the rows keep their own padding. Its words sit the card's padding in from its edge, and a row's hover tile keeps clear of the corners. 2026-10-22, "the padding around the list menus ... must be spacious": the words 24px in, the tiles 16px in on every side. The card adds half the inset above and below and each tile takes the other half inside its row, so the first and last tiles sit one inset from the edge, two tiles sit one inset apart, and the rows keep their 64px rhythm. 2026-10-24, the owner: "I want the padding to be less and the list items to be spacious to improve click area ... 4px padding is decent": the inset is 4px, a link row's box is its tile (one inset from the card's edges, its words still the padding in), so the whole tile is the target and nothing outside it is. The card adds the inset above and below and two rows sit one inset apart; each row keeps 64px.

---

## Settings row (`settings-row`)

A row with a label and an in-place control: a switch, a select or a value.

### Use when

- a setting with a switch
- a setting with a select
- a labeled value with a hint

### Not when

- a row that opens another page: use [`row-action`](parts/row-action.md)

`--button-radius` `--card-inset` `--color-on-surface` `--color-on-surface-muted` `--field-chevron-gap` `--row-padding-block` `--size-icon` `--size-touch-comfortable` `--slider-max-width`

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.settings-row` `.settings-label` `.settings-hint` (typed on your own element)
- Styled in: `styles/picker.css`, `styles/primitives.css`, `styles/settings-rows.css`

### Owner's note

Label and description at the start, the control at the end. The row grammar adds the padding and the hairline; with that padding this minimum is the 48px floor, and most rows are taller.

## Stat tiles (`stat-tiles`)

A tile per figure: the value large over its word in muted ink.

### Use when

- figures on a dashboard
- costs and spend totals

### Not when

- a list of rows: use [`card-group`](parts/card-group.md)

### Where it is drawn

- Classes: `.stat-tiles` (typed on your own element)
- Styled in: `styles/primitives.css`

### Owner's note

A figure on a dashboard: a tile per stat, its value large over its word in muted ink, two columns on a phone and four from 40rem. The owner, 2026-10-27: the Costs page's stat pills became boxes, no pill for a figure. In a card a tile sits the card's padding in, so its corner is the card's less that padding (--card-content-radius, concentric), and it takes the overlay tone, as the card's chips do. On the 8pt grid: 16px in, a 24px value line and a 24px label line, 80px a tile. The value is the title step at regular weight, under the page's total it explains (owner, 2026-10-27: the heading-size medium value "competes with the main cost number"). Put .stat-tiles on the list and .stat-tile on each item, with .stat-tile-value and .stat-tile-label inside. Used by the Costs page (analytics.astro, costsPage.ts) and the Health page's summary (settings/health.astro).

## PlayingBars

Import `@singularityfm/design-system/PlayingBars`. No part covers it yet, so `ds find` does not name it.

### Props of PlayingBars

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className?` | `string` | - | For placing the bars where they stand, or a hook a page's rule finds them by (the reader's cover button sizes them to its glyph). Never their look. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop. |
| `slot?` | `string` | - | Astro places the bars in its parent's slot with it; it is not an attribute of the element. |

---

## RowExit

Import `@singularityfm/design-system/RowExit`. No part covers it yet, so `ds find` does not name it.

### Props of RowExit

| Name | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className?` | `string` | `""` | For placing the row (its own layout). Never how it leaves. An Astro page passes className too: @astrojs/react drops a `class` prop before the component sees it. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | - | The row's content. |
